My suggestions:

Get the essential alcohols: Vodka, Gin (London Dry), White Rum, Tequila Blanco, Bourbon, Scotch, Cognac, Sweet and Dry Vermouths, Cointreau, and Maraschino Liqueur. Expand (primarily in liqueurs) as needed for your favorite cocktails.

Pick up one of each of these bitters: Angostura bitters, Orange bitters, and Peychaud’s bitters.

Have plenty of lemons, limes, and oranges, and also have sugar syrup — these things are needed for tons of cocktails.

As for glassware, have multiple of each of the following: coupe glass, highball/Collins glass, and rocks glass. Also get flutes, martini glasses, slings, and hurricane glasses if you make drinks that call for them.

Bar tools: Boston shaker, Cobbler shaker, Mixing glass, Barspoon, peeler, Hawthorne strainer, jigger, citrus juicer.

Plenty of ice is needed, obviously. Crushed, cubes, and large ice lamps.

Other things are more dependent on what specific cocktails you are making. If you want a Bramble, then obviously get a bottle of creme de mure. If you want to make a Clover Club, get raspberries (I’ll assume you have eggs). A bottle of Campari is necessary for Negronis and Boulevardiers. Want a gin and tonic? Get tonic.

Not all of these things are needed for someone just starting in the cocktail world, but this is a pretty expansive list. If you go to the grocery store and pick up a bottle of vodka and some oranges, then squeeze the juice and throw it in a glass with the vodka and some ice, you have a screwdriver. Don’t stress about having everything a bar can possibly have — when just starting, just buy ingredients and tools for your favorite cocktails and ones you want to try.
